chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather, may the prayers of Allah be upon them, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah created Islam, so He made for it a space/land, and He made for it a light, and He made for it a fortress, and He made for it a helper.'

So as for its space/land, it is the Quran; and as for its light, it is Wisdom; and as for its fortress, it is the Good (al-Ma'ruf); and as for its helpers, it is I, and my People of the Household, and our Shia.

So love my People of the Household and their Shia and their helpers. For when I was ascended to the lowest heaven, Jibril (peace be upon him) introduced me to the inhabitants of the heaven. Allah entrusted the love of me, and the love of my People of the Household and their Shia, into the hearts of the angels, so it is a deposit with them until the Day of Resurrection.

Then he brought me down to the people of the earth and introduced me to the people of the earth. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, entrusted the love of me, and the love of my People of the Household and their Shia, into the hearts of the believers of my community. Thus, the believers of my community preserve my deposit regarding my People of the Household until the Day of Resurrection.

So, if a man from my community were to worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for his lifetime, the days of the world, then he meets Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as hating my People of the Household and my Shia, Allah will not open his chest for anything except for Hypocrisy.
ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars of Islam according to this hadith and who are its designated helpers?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi* articulates the metaphysical architecture of Islam, identifying the Quran, Wisdom, Goodness, and the Prophet's household as its essential pillars. It highlights the concept of *Wadi'ah* (divine trust), where love for the Ahl al-Bayt is embedded in the hearts of angels and believers, serving as the ultimate criterion for the acceptance of worship. Consequently, the text establishes that enduring enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt reduces even prolonged devotion to mere hypocrisy (*Nifaq*).

en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd al-‘Azim from ‘Abd Allah al-Hassani from Abu Ja’far al-Thani (a.s.) from his father from his grandfather (a.s.) who has said the following: “Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said that the Messenger of Allah said, ‘Allah created Islam and made for it a backyard and front-yard, a light, a fortress and supporter.
Its backyard and front-yard are the Holy Quran. Wisdom is its light. Lawfulness is its fortress. My Ahl al-Bayt (my family), our Shi’a (followers) and I are its supporters.

You must love my Ahl al-Bayt (members of my family), their followers (Shi’a) and their supporters. When I was taken to heaven above the earth, Gibril introduced me to its inhabitants. Allah entrusted the love for me, my Ahl al-Bayt and their followers (Shi’a) to the hearts of the angels. It is with them in trust until the Day of Judgment.

Then I was brought to earth and he introduced me to the inhabitants of earth. Allah entrusted the love for me, my Ahl al-Bayt and their followers (Shi’a) to the hearts of the believers of my people. They will keep my trust and the trust of my Ahl al-Bayt until the Day of Judgment.

One must know that if a man of my people would worship Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, all the time of his life and then would meet Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, while hating my Ahl al-Bayt and my followers (Shi’a) Allah will not open his chest for anything but in hypocrisy.’”
